In coil A, a current as shown in Figure B is passed; at t＝0 the current direction is clockwise (as shown by the arrow in the figure). Then which of the following statements is correct (　　)

ready2_open_rewrite.resolved_question_text: According to Figure A and Figure B, during the time interval t1～t2, what is the direction of the induced current in coil B?
ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: First describe the images: in Figure A, two concentric circular closed coils can be seen, the inner one is coil A and the outer one is coil B; the current arrow above coil A points to the right along the circumference, indicating that the positive direction shown in the figure is clockwise. Figure B is a graph of the current i in A changing with time t; the straight line decreases from a positive value, becomes zero at time t1, and between t1 and t2 is below the horizontal axis and continues downward, indicating that the actual current direction in A is opposite to the arrow in Figure A, namely counterclockwise, and that the magnitude of the current gradually increases. Then reason: the counterclockwise current produces magnetic flux perpendicular to the paper surface and outward in the region where coil B is located; during t1～t2 this outward magnetic flux increases. According to Lenz's law, the induced current in coil B should produce a magnetic field perpendicular to the paper surface and inward, to hinder the increase of the outward magnetic flux. By the right-hand rule, the current direction corresponding to producing a magnetic field perpendicular to the paper surface and inward in a circular coil is clockwise. Therefore, the direction of the induced current in coil B is clockwise.
